newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber seen lower on currencies, low demand.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber seen lower on currencies, low demand.

text.p: Currency volatility across the region, slow demand and concerns over government stocks will continue to weigh down the Thai rubber market next week, trade sources said on Friday.
A weakening Indonesian rupiah and Malaysia's ringgit prompted concerns among local exporters that buyers could turn to those markets for cheaper products.
The rupiah fell to a historic low of 2,940 against the dollar on Friday afternoon following the central bank's move on Thursday to scrap its intervention plan.
"We are not happy about this at all. The falling rupiah or ringgit could attract buyers from this market," said a Bangkok-based trader.
"I expect the price to move in a narrow range with a downward bias next week," he said.
The trade in the market this week was moderate with Chinese buyers absent. Michelin came into the market for October RSS3 but bought less than 100 tonnes per day, traders said.
Japan's Marubeni also sought January-March shipments but bought only moderate amounts, they said.
"The demand situation was not that exciting but more supplies are entering the market," he said.
The benchmark RSS3 was indicated around 91.00-92.00 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok for October shipment fand 93.50 US cents for January.
Lingering market talk about possible selling of government stocks which exceeded 70,000 tonnes continued to keep the market on edge despite repeated denials from the authorities, traders said.
"The market seemed to be convinced that the government is considering selling the stock. It could be just a matter of time," said a Hat Yai trader.
